summary: Oman lets GCC nationals enter freely and waives visas for stays of up to 14 days for 78 nationalities, including the EU, US, UK and Canada, and for 24 more whose citizens live in or hold a visa for the US, Canada, Australia, the UK, a Schengen country or Japan, while the Royal Oman Police eVisa covers longer tourist stays; other nationalities need a sponsored or embassy visa.

tips.text: The Foreign Ministry says the 14-day visa-free entry requires a return ticket, a confirmed hotel booking, health insurance and enough money for the stay, and cannot be extended. For longer trips, apply for a visa on the Royal Oman Police eVisa website before travel.

The UK FCDO says wadis (dry riverbeds) are prone to flash flooding after heavy rain from October to March. Check the forecast before visiting a wadi and avoid places where heavy rain is expected, and for at least one day afterwards.

The UK FCDO says road trips to the desert and mountains can be dangerous unless you are in a well-equipped four-wheel-drive vehicle; travel in convoy if possible, carry water and a phone, and leave your plans with someone.
The UK FCDO says to dress modestly in public areas, including malls, with the tops of arms and legs (below the knee) covered, and not to wear swimwear in public except on tourist beaches or at pools.

The UK FCDO says visitors can buy and drink alcohol only in licensed venues such as hotels, restaurants and clubs (legal age 21). Drinking or being drunk in public and drink-driving are illegal, and any alcohol found in a driver's system can bring a fine and possible imprisonment.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Oman?
faq.answer: GCC citizens do not need a visa. 78 nationalities — including the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, Japan and China — can enter visa-free for up to 14 days with a return ticket, a confirmed hotel booking, health insurance and enough money for the stay; 24 more can if they live in or hold a visa for the US, Canada, Australia, the UK, a Schengen country or Japan. For longer tourist stays the Royal Oman Police issues an unsponsored 30-day eVisa. Other nationalities need a sponsored or embassy visa.

faq.question: How does Oman's 14-day visa-free entry work?
faq.answer: The Foreign Ministry admits eligible nationalities without a visa for stays of up to 14 days, which cannot be extended or turned into a residence visa. The visitor needs a passport valid for at least six months, a return ticket, a confirmed hotel booking, health insurance and enough money for the stay. For anything longer, apply for a visa on the Royal Oman Police eVisa website (evisa.rop.gov.om).

faq.question: How much does the Oman eVisa cost?
faq.answer: The Royal Oman Police eVisa website lists an unsponsored tourist eVisa for a 10-day or a 30-day visit (the stay can be extended by the same length, the first time online). No official source we could read states the fee. Apply through the Royal Oman Police eVisa website (evisa.rop.gov.om).

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Oman?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states whether Oman admits travellers on Israeli passports.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Oman?
faq.answer: No official source names a best time to visit. The UK FCDO says wadis are prone to flash flooding after heavy rain from October to March, tropical cyclones sometimes affect Oman in July and August, and extreme heat has caused deaths from dehydration and heat exhaustion.
